If the battery is dead, and you jump start it, it is possible that the computer for the instruments did not boot. Got it. Bottom first.
---POST---
The worst of the dash rattles, for me, was below the center dash mesh screen speaker cover. I don't have a speaker there, but directly under where the speaker would be is a torx screw that fastens the speaker "bucket" housing to the aluminum support below it. This screw was loose and made a lot of noise. Tightening this down the rattle was gone. You don't have to pull the display, just remove the mesh screen on the center dash and pull the speaker if you have one then tighten down from above.
---POST---
I've been visiting different dealerships over 8 times in the last 4 months to try to resolve a persistent rattle that's inside the instrument cluster. Each time they would sort of fix it, but then it worsens after. Does anyone have instructions to take out the instrument cluster?

I'm also trying to resolve another rattle inside the center speaker, and I remember someone made a thread on opening that up too. If someone remembers which thread that is, that would be great!
---POST---
If you grab ahold of the top part of the dash where it humps up over the instrument cluster, and rock it up and down does that recreate the noise?

For the dash speaker, get some 3/8" foam speaker sealing tape. Pop off the cover (it just snaps on and off) by prying an edge up and then lifting upward. There are a half dozen clips holding it in. Run speaker tape around the underside perimeter between the clips and pop the cover back on. The tape causes there to be more tension on the clips and stops the buzzing.

Thread 769103 Content:
 So i got off work today and my car was dead so i jump started it. Everything is working fine accept the instrument cluster will not come on. Car drives fine everything is working no power to the cluster. Checked fuse box under the hood no bad fuses please tell me what i need to do had the car for 3-4 yrs with no issues
---POST---
replace the battery
---POST---
If the battery is dead, and you jump start it, it is possible that the computer for the instruments did not boot. This boot normally happens when you open the door before getting into the vehicle so it is ready for the start. Have you turned off the vehicle and restarted without jumping? When you open a door with the vehicle off, does the dash show mileage for a few seconds? If not, your instrument/nav computer is not booting. Maybe the battery is still low of charge. Agree with Mmr1 , replace battery.

Clarify please, the entire cluster or just portions of it?

Sounds like an intermittent short somewhere.

---POST---
Got it. Bottom first.
---POST---
The worst of the dash rattles, for me, was below the center dash mesh screen speaker cover. I don't have a speaker there, but directly under where the speaker would be is a torx screw that fastens the speaker "bucket" housing to the aluminum support below it. This screw was loose and made a lot of noise. Tightening this down the rattle was gone. You don't have to pull the display, just remove the mesh screen on the center dash and pull the speaker if you have one then tighten down from above.
---POST---
I've been visiting different dealerships over 8 times in the last 4 months to try to resolve a persistent rattle that's inside the instrument cluster. Each time they would sort of fix it, but then it worsens after. Does anyone have instructions to take out the instrument cluster?

I'm also trying to resolve another rattle inside the center speaker, and I remember someone made a thread on opening that up too. If someone remembers which thread that is, that would be great!
---POST---
If you grab ahold of the top part of the dash where it humps up over the instrument cluster, and rock it up and down does that recreate the noise?

For the dash speaker, get some 3/8" foam speaker sealing tape. Pop off the cover (it just snaps on and off) by prying an edge up and then lifting upward. There are a half dozen clips holding it in. Run speaker tape around the underside perimeter between the clips and pop the cover back on. The tape causes there to be more tension on the clips and stops the buzzing.

Thread 817321 (Odometer / Cluster Cloning):

2) I read that it's plug and play after the new cluster arrives. WILL (or COULD) SWAPPING OUT A CLUSTER CAUSE *ANY* ISSUES with immobilizer / not starting, warning lights, codes, etc.?
3) I understand this service itself is legal in the US, since I'm not trying to change the actual mileage of the car or do anything fraudulent, but does anyone know if a disclosure will be required or if there will be issues with the title since it's not the odometer the car came with? I want to stay on the right side of the law, obviously.

Thread 832313 Content:
 Hello, I think in the forum already have various topics talking about this situation, but I can't seem to find any answers for my problem.
Thanks in advance for any answers and help.
I have a w204 estate (S204) 2009 pre-facelift, and I have the cluster below:

This is my steering wheel. (4 button version)
I would like to know if someone could help me out. I am interested in changing my stock cluster for any of the models of the clusters attached below (I take suggestions as well), doing this do I need to change the steering wheel as well ? I would like to know how difficult would this process be, if it would need any coding as I would be buying used parts or would be like plug and play and that's it.

---POST---
Replacing the instrument cluster, specially for the updated one, is not plug and play. If you have access online, it will not go through since the cluster does not belong to that VIN. But in any case, the SSID and mileage needs to be changed. Also coding needs to be done and finally you will need to write the service data.

Hi Henry, noticed that ur using audio 20. How do u set the time n date since there's no setting for it inside the new cluster menu?

Thanks in advance.
---POST---
Any advise?
Anyone with info can share?
---POST---
Quote:
Originally Posted by Trdspec86 
Hi Henry, noticed that ur using audio 20. How do u set the time n date since there's no setting for it inside the new cluster menu?
I've also fitted a FL cluster n can't adjust the time n date.
Thanks in advance.
By default time and language settings are hidden and need to set from Audio then it will sync to speedometer cluster automatically.
It is easy to code the cluster to re-enable time and language settings,
change time/date format, 24->12, yyyy/mm/dd, dd/mm/yyyy etc.
For languages, FL cluster already supported most western and asian languages, and support some middle east.
You can code it to display all supported languages, restrict to some western and asian, or no asian.
